# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-27

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero nails the value prop in one breath (the "47 + 28 = 76" example is
genuinely great), so I'd start reading — but I'd lose trust fast: the page tells
me it's MIT-0 at the top and Apache 2.0 at the bottom, leads its hero with an
apology about a downgraded number ("Repinned from v2 0.9857"), and buries the
"Results" section under a wall of 12 cards full of acronyms I've never heard of
(CCTU, VeriCoT, CRANE, FoVer, PREM). Net: I'd skim, smell "internal lab notebook
dressed as a landing page," and probably close the tab unless I was already an
EBM person.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradiction — hero badge + meta say "MIT-0", footer says "Apache 2.0 License". A stranger who cares about license (i.e. anyone evaluating adoption) sees the project contradict itself on the single most load-bearing trust fact.
2. Acronym wall in Results ("What we measured") — 12 dense cards keyed on unexplained insider names (CCTU, VeriCoT, CRANE, EstimationVerifier, PRM-BiasBench, HalluGuard v3, FoVer, k=5). A stranger skims none of them, so the project's strongest evidence reads as noise.
3. Suspiciously-perfect numbers with no sample size — "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0", "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks", "Zero false positives", "2.0× speedup, identical losses". Perfect 1.0 / 60-of-60 with no n or CI reads as fabricated, which poisons the credible numbers next to them.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- No HARD threshold is crossed (largest bento body ~80 words < 120; result cards are tiny < 60; footer is one line < 100; no single grid has > 20 cards). I'm flagging soft skim-fatigue instead:
- Results grid ("What we measured") — 12 cards — recommend cutting to the ~5–6 strongest. Twelve near-identical meter cards, each fronted by an acronym, is a wall a stranger scrolls past.
- Hero stats-bar — 5 items (4 stats + a full paragraph "Recent progress" card jammed in) — the stat row is overloaded and mixes a 2.25rem number row with a prose card; recommend ≤4 clean stats, move the paragraph out.
- Nav bar — 12 link items + 2 buttons — that's a cluttered top-of-page; recommend ~5 (Get Started, Results, Quick Start, Paper, GitHub). On mobile they're hidden entirely (`display:none`), so the count only hurts desktop.
- Cumulative page length — ~32 cards across 5 grids (Problem 2, How 4, Features 7, Results 12, Writing 7) — long for a landing page even though no one section trips the cap.

### Internal jargon
- Hero stat "382 Completed milestones" — a "milestone" is an internal project-management unit; to a stranger this is a vanity number with no meaning about whether the tool is good.
- Hero stat / "Recent progress" card — "FoVer", "5-seed", "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857" — dataset name + internal methodology + revision history that a first-time reader cannot parse.
- Results card "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" — "publication gate" is internal process language; it also reads as "we set our own bar and just barely cleared it."
- Results cards — "EstimationVerifier", "VeriCoT", "CRANE", "PRM-BiasBench-style", "HalluGuard v3", "CCTU", "k=5 ensemble" — a stack of undefined proper nouns/acronyms; none is glossed.
- Features "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" card — "PREM / Process-Reward Energy Model", "TTC", "intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning" — the single most opaque card on the page; it is nearly content-free to a stranger and vague even to an expert.
- Features "Multi-step reasoning" — "AND-composed" — unexplained.
- Preprint section — "paper-v6", "checked-in experiment artifacts", "continuous-integration checkout", "non-operator environment", "operator-initiated upload" — internal-role vocabulary ("operator") a stranger doesn't share; "pending upload" also tells them the paper isn't actually on arXiv yet.
- Blog cards — "Deep Think" (line: "Five FATAL Findings Three Deep Think Rounds Missed"), "NTK"/"arXiv:2601.18753" — niche; fine for a blog index but adds to the insider feel.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Hero "Recent progress" card — "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit" — this is retrospective/changelog narrative on the landing page, and it's the *first* substantive sentence a reader hits. Honesty belongs in the linked blog post, not as the hero's lead credibility line.
- Hero stat — "382 Completed milestones" — milestone counting surfaced as a headline metric.
- Versioned names in card prose — "HalluGuard v3", "paper-v6" — version suffixes are internal status, not user-facing.

### Inconsistencies
- LICENSE: "MIT-0" (meta description line 7, hero badge line 291, hero sub) vs "Apache 2.0 License" (footer line 766). Direct contradiction.
- "FoVer" means two opposite things: the headline dataset where Carnot scores 0.9131 AUROC (high = good) AND a "0.125 FoVer baseline" (low) that EstimationVerifier's 0.90 beats. A stranger can't tell whether FoVer is the good result or the thing being beaten.
- Metric naming: headline is "AUROC" (0.9131, 0.91) but the SVAMP card says "AUC" (0.90 AUC). Mixing AUC/AUROC across cards looks sloppy and invites "do they know which metric they ran?"
- Two different "0.91" AUROC figures (FoVer verification 0.9131 vs prompt-injection classifier 0.91) sit close together with no disambiguation; easy to conflate.
- The "47 + 28" worked example is "= 76" in the hero, problem intro, "Whole-answer check" card, and code sample — but the "One-word-at-a-time" card uses "= 7". Likely intentional (mid-generation), but it reads as an inconsistency at a glance.

### Missing essentials
- License is effectively MISSING because it's contradictory (see above) — the one fact an adopter must know is unreliable.
- Who maintains it / community signal: only "© 2026 Ian Blenke" in the footer. No team, contributors, contact, Discord/issues link, or adoption signal (stars, downloads). A single-maintainer project with no community cue is a risk a stranger weighs when deciding to depend on it.
- Trust path for the numbers: the page asserts "Every number below is backed by a checked-in experiment artifact" but no individual card links to its artifact — the stranger is asked to take it on faith, right next to the perfect-looking numbers.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (Results) — a perfect 1.0, meter at 100%, no sample size.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (Results) — 100% on a small n=60, no CI.
- "Zero false positives" (Dogfooding blog card) — perfect claim.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (Results) — "identical" is suspiciously exact.
- "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" — round number labeled as just clearing an internal bar; reads as threshold-gamed.
- Mitigating note: "99.3% of wrong code flagged" carries a denominator (HumanEval-164) and isn't perfect, which is more credible — the perfect numbers stand out against it.

### Structural / rendering defects (first-impression credibility)
- Hero (lines 304–316): the "Recent progress" `r-card` is nested INSIDE the flex `stats-bar` as a 5th flex child, and there's an extra unbalanced `</div>`. Likely renders as a card awkwardly wedged into the stat row. The paragraph also uses class `r-desc`, which is not defined in the CSS, so it's unstyled.
- Features (lines 494–501): the 7th card ("Test-Time Compute & PREM") sits OUTSIDE the `.bento-grid` (the grid `</div>` closes at line 494 before this card). So "Seven capabilities" visually renders as 6 grid cards + 1 orphaned full-width card — a botched-edit tell.
- Rust code sample uses `<span class="num">` (lines 643, 652) but `.num` is undefined in CSS → those numerals render unstyled. Minor, but it's in a code window meant to look polished.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero problem framing is excellent: "LLMs predict. They don't check." + the concrete "47 + 28 = 76 (correct: 75)" example communicates the entire value prop in seconds, no jargon.
- "Extract → Check → Repair" is a clean, honest three-step mental model, and the Quick Start shows real, short, copy-pasteable code with a clean `pip install carnot-ebm` path.
